text:
kevin: Heads-up: I hit a stale-read during a handoff + soft-evict experiment. sketching thread so we can agree an interface.

olivia: can you outline the repro sequence?

kevin: W writes -> node A soft-evicts prefix (keeps tombstones) -> snapshotter produces S (lagging, missing W) -> node B claims and loads S -> client reads before W.

raj: this is the demote vs snapshot freshness gap we've feared. snapshots currently trust manifest timestamp only.

maria: thought: attach a small monotonic "residency_token" to demote events and persist it under a cheap key. snapshot manifests include token_seen. claimant validates token_seen >= current_token.

sahil: similar to "fence" ideas, but call it token to stress monotonicity. on demote do: INCR /meta/evict_token/<prefix> -> new_token. snapshotter reads token at start and records token_seen in manifest.

andrew: claim-time algorithm: 1) read current token T1; 2) grab claim lease; 3) re-read token T2; 4) if T2 > snapshot.token_seen then reject snapshot and apply delta log or rebuild; else proceed. ensures no race if demote happens during claim.

olivia: delta-first fallback is important to avoid full rebuild storms. prefer: try small delta apply (log since snapshot), if delta unavailable or too big escalate to full rebuild. add backpressure if many rejects occur.

raj: compatibility: older snapshots won't have token_seen. treat missing as 0. if current token > 0 claimant must reject. migration note: roll out snapshotter + claimant together.

maria: GC: token keys need cleanup when prefix retired. plan: GC job that deletes /meta/evict_token/<prefix> once manifest=DELETED && tombstones expired OR a TTL of 30d since last demote. safer to GC only after tombstone window.

kevin: performance: per-demote INCR is cheap (small write). ci run we did: 2k demotes, token bumps ~2k, snapshot rejects 0.3%, median delta apply 1.9ms. ci report: https://ci/reports/9788-evict-token-run

sahil: operational knobs: metric names snapshot_token_rejects, delta_apply_latency_ms, token_gc_deleted_count. add alert when reject_rate > 1% sustained.

andrew: one more corner: compaction can remove tombstones referenced by older snapshots, forcing rejects anyway. token helps make the reason explicit (token mismatch) vs mystery stale reads.

olivia: test plan: chaos test that injects snapshot delay and concurrent demote/claim; verify linearizability for reads where write happened before demote. add property-based checks.

kevin: I'll draft a short RFC: key layout (/meta/evict_token/<prefix>), manifest change (token_seen string), claim precheck pseudocode, delta-first fallback, GC policy, metrics and playbook. aiming prototype next sprint.

maria: :+1: include rollout steps and cmp notes for older snapshot loaders.

ci-bot: quick perf summary appended: 2k cycles, 0.3% rejects, median delta 1.9ms, p95 6.2ms. full: https://ci/reports/9788-evict-token-run

olivia: great, thanks Kevin. please also add a safety circuit-breaker to limit concurrent delta fetches if rejects spike.

kevin: will do, posting RFC link when ready.
